newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine busmaker seeks foreign strategic investor.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine busmaker seeks foreign strategic investor.

text.p: Ukraine's only busmaker, Lvivsky Avtobusny Zavod (LAZ) is seeking a strategic foreign investor to help it revive production of buses and trolley buses, a senior government official said on Wednesday.

Bohdan Nychai, head of the carmaking department at the Ministry for Machine Building (Military Complex and Conversion), said that foreign investment of about $50 million would be the only way to update ageing plant in the western Ukrainian city of Lviv.
"This company has really good prospects taking into account the old pool of buses in Ukraine and elsewhere in the former Soviet Union," Nychai told Reuters. "But it must be modernised."

The government decided last October to give 26 percent of LAZ's shares to foreign investors while 25 percent will remain at state hands. The remaining 49 pecent will be sold for privatisation certificates, partly to LAZ's workforce.
LAZ, founded in 1945, employs 7,000 workers but the government believes the workforce will fall to 4,000-5,000 after modernisation.
Last year LAZ production halved to 1,053 buses from 2,148 buses in 1995. Sales fell to 67 million hryvnias ($35 million) last year from 86.5 million ($47 million) in 1995.

The buses last year were mostly sold to Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. Nychai said Ukraine usually buys about one third of LAZ's buses and blamed poor municipal budgets for the fall in bus production.

In Soviet times the plant produced 14,000 buses annually -- mostly for inter-city routes -- while city buses were mostly made at the LIAZ plant in Likino near Moscow or imported from Hungary's Ikarus.

LAZ chief executive Stepan Davydyak told Reuters earlier this week that the company had sent proposals to 25 foreign companies to become strategic investors. They include two German carmakers, Daimler-Benz AG's Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen AG, Swedish Volvo and Italian Fiat.
But both Nychai and Davydyak say Renault is the favoured partner, given a long history of cooperation between it and LAZ.
"We are looking desperately for a strategic investor," Davydyak said. "We are now studying the possibility of Renault becoming a strategic investor. We are looking for the final reply from them."
Renault is already supplying LAZ with powerful bus engines and given LAZ $600,000 interest-free credit.
Nychai said LAZ will concentrate in future on production of buses and trolley buses with a large capacity.
The company has launched production of a diesel city bus with 120-passenger capacity, an intercity bus for 49 passengers and a 108-passenger trolley bus.
Last year it produced five city "super-buses" with 191-passenger capacity each.
"This plant gradually will be shifting to the production of larger-capacity city buses," Nychai said. "They are the very future of the city transport."

Privatisation has been slow in Ukraine, and the sale to strategic investors of stakes in a list of large companies drawn up by the government has been held up by a dispute with parliament about investment rules.
